thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert — streaming p99 latency spike in us-west-2 (service: inference-stream). Metric: p99 = 2.8s (baseline 220ms). Correctable ECC errors rising on gpu-node-34.*. Automated routing fallback not yet triggered. Incident severity: P1.

Anna (oncall): I'm oncall. assigning myself. initial triage: are we seeing increased errors or just tail latency? @Sam @James please grab node health + runtime traces.

James (sre): looking. syslogs show repeated correctable ECC on node gpu-node-34, thermal trips observed ~ 03:12 UTC. p95 only moved to ~420ms but p99 exploded. pulling dmesg now.

Sam (eng-runtime): I've opened the serving traces. KV cache misses jump correlated with node-34 churn. streaming workers on that node show repeated stall events. grabbing stack traces.

Lee (ml-ops): model-side: no config changes. traffic distribution shows 18% of streaming sessions pinned to node-34 due to shard affinity. fallback model variants are healthy in other regions.

James (sre): dmesg snippet: ```
[03:12:08] Correctable ECC error on GPU 1
[03:12:08] GPU thermal threshold reached, freq reduced
[03:12:09] GPU driver recovered, but repeated events
```

Sam (eng-runtime): runtime logs: ```
2026-03-15T03:12:10Z WARN stall_detected session=abc123 worker=gpu-node-34:stream-7 tail_ms=2800
2026-03-15T03:12:11Z ERROR kv_fetch_timeout key=chat-prefix-xyz
```

Anna (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) take gpu-node-34 out of serving pool, 2) route affected sessions to fallback model variant in us-east-1, 3) enable increased parallelism on remaining nodes to absorb traffic. Who can execute drain? @James please.

James (sre): starting drain. running: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-34 && kubectl drain gpu-node-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30```

Sam (eng-runtime): before we fully drain, add quick routing rule to avoid new sticky sessions landing on node-34: ```PATCH /v1/routing/policies/streaming
{ "match": {"region":"us-west-2","prefer_node":"-gpu-node-34"} }``` will push traffic off. I'll deploy that now.

Sam (eng-runtime): pushed routing change. confirm: new sessions avoid node-34. existing streaming sessions will be gracefully failed over per fallback policy.

Lee (ml-ops): triggering model fallback for active sessions that hit stall threshold (>=1500ms) to quantized variant `tiny-v2-q4`. Doing a gradual ramp 10% -> 50%.

Ryan (customer-ops): customer impact: alerting shows 3 customers (acct-111, acct-227, acct-305) with spike in error rates and user-visible streaming pauses. SLA p99 breached for them. preparing outreach.

Elaine (product): thanks. prioritize outreach to acct-111 + acct-227 first (highest traffic). Ryan, please use the incident template with mention of degraded streaming + mitigation steps. cc security if data residency impacted.

James (sre): drain progress: pods evicted 12/14, 2 stuck due to local cache. forcing delete on stuck pods.```kubectl delete pod pod-xyz --grace-period=5 --force```

Sam (eng-runtime): KV cache warmup in other nodes is still ramping. I'm manually warming top prefixes for the 3 impacted customers to reduce early tail. running cache prefetch script: ```/opt/redeploy/prefetch_prefixes.sh acct-111 acct-227 acct-305```

Anna (oncall): timeline note: page at 03:11 UTC, routing change at 03:15 UTC, drain started 03:16 UTC. need to confirm p99 returning to baseline before declaring mitigated.

James (sre): node-34 hardware: ECC correctable count = 120 in last 10m, temp peaked at 84C. Fan speed oscillation logs show irregular PWM around events. suspect flaky fan or transient power rail. I propose we quarantine node for deeper hardware runbook and open hardware ticket.

Sam (eng-runtime): p99 reporting now 480ms globally for streaming; us-west-2 p99 = 560ms. big improvement from 2.8s but still above baseline. p95 is 320ms.

Lee (ml-ops): model fallbacks are serving ~22% of streaming traffic now. quality monitoring shows minor uptick in hallucination metric for tiny-v2-q4 but within alert tolerances.

Anna (oncall): declare customer-impacting but partially mitigated. continuing live mitigation. assigning hardware and postmortem: owner James. postmortem timeline owner: Sam.

Ryan (customer-ops): sent first outreach to acct-111 and acct-227 at 03:28 UTC. template: "We saw degraded streaming performance between 03:11–03:20 UTC affecting streaming p99. We rerouted traffic and quarantined a GPU node; mitigations are in place." will update after final resolution.

Elaine (product): thumbs up. please include expected follow-up: ETA for fix and whether any data loss.

James (sre): opened HW ticket with datacenter -> ticket #DC-48291. RMA recommended if ECC persists after power cycle. Scheduling tech to perform fan check and power rail probe.

Sam (eng-runtime): monitoring: enabling additional tracing for stall reasons for next 6 hours. I'll also add temporary circuit-breaker lowering burst concurrency for streaming sessions touching high-ECC nodes to reduce re-triggering.

Anna (oncall): handing oncall to James for overnight; I need to step out for 30m. James please continue watch and coordinate with DC. I'll stay available via DM.

James (sre): ack takeover. will keep thread updated. current status: mitigated (reduced user impact), hw quarantine + postmortem follow-up required. next steps: RMA if fan/power check fails, review shard affinity logic to avoid >15% traffic pinned to single node, add automatic routing fallback threshold at p99>1s.

Sam (eng-runtime): filing a quick PR for routing fallback threshold: ```if p99(region) > 1000ms -> mark region fallback true``` aiming for deployment in next 2 hours.

Lee (ml-ops): follow-up: we'll run evals on tiny-v2-q4 for customer-critical prompts to ensure no regression before making it a permanent fallback.

Ryan (customer-ops): will send final customer update once p99 stable for 30m.

Anna (oncall): logging timeline to incident tracker, adding tags: gpu, ecc, thermal, streaming, p99, hw-quarantine. Good job team.

James (sre): last check at 03:46 UTC: us-west-2 p99 = 350ms, global p99 = 300ms. Keeping watch. will file postmortem draft tomorrow.

Sam (eng-runtime): note: prefer we also add a runbook step to pre-warm KV for failover target when node is drained — reduces immediate tail. will add to runbook PR.

Anna (oncall): closing active paging loop for now; thread remains for follow-up.
